meta.title: MPSS Proof Ledger
meta.headline: Type safety in MPSS, as stated, is false
meta.standfirst: Every numbered result in the paper's metatheory, machine-checked in Agda under --safe — no postulates, no holes, no termination pragmas. Colour is the verdict; hover a result and everything it rests on lights up, what its proof cites and what its statement is built from. Transitivity elimination and progress hold for the paper's calculus with nothing assumed. Conjecture 8 is false as stated, and so are Lemmas 6 and 7 and preservation (MPSS.Conj8Refuted): contexts need only be prevalid, so a context may define R ≡ ω ω with ω = λs≤⊤. λx≤(s s). (s s), where R is well-formed and behaves as the recursive type R ≡ λx≤R.R; with δ = λx≤R. x x, the divergent δ δ is expected below R and is below nothing but ⊤. Whether they hold once context annotations must be well-formed is open. Two more of the paper's propositions are false; one is repaired and proved, the other repaired in a different form and proved.
footer: Conjecture 8, Lemmas 6 and 7, Theorem 5: refuted as stated, in a prevalid context with an ill-formed annotation (MPSS.Conj8Refuted)
Propositions 17 and 18: refuted as printed, repaired forms proved (↻)
Lemmas 1, 2 and 31: open as printed, a variant proved (↻)

items.anchor: Conjecture 8 and type safety · what is left
items.html:
Refuted as stated (MPSS.Conj8Refuted), with Lemmas 6 and 7 and preservation: a prevalid context may define a recursive type, R ≡ ω ω, because prevalidity does not ask annotations to be well-formed.

The obvious repair is to ask that — Pv-Ctx and Pv-EqA with a well-formedness premise on the annotation. Whether the conjecture and type safety hold then is open. The same instance fails as soon as any well-formed term behaves as R does, which needs a type-level looping combinator (the paper's §6 expects term-level ones); and a proof cannot be a rank induction, since the domain order already cycles at the type of the polymorphic identity, T = λy≤⊤. λx≤y. y: T T is well-formed and its domain is T.

Recorded on the way, each with where it breaks: the nesting-depth measure, the narrowing route (its intermediate points are ill-formed at dependent bounds), the substitution route run as an algorithm (valid on every instance tried, measure not found).

items.anchor: Lemma 2 and Lemma 1 · the diamond and commutation, as printed
items.html:
Open for the paper's relation, and nothing depends on them any more: both are proved for the reduction with the promotion premise at the empty stack, which has the same closure, and Theorem 3 follows for the paper's calculus. The printed induction on Lemma 2 cannot be rescued by a measure (MPSS.NoMeasure).

What is known of the original diamond: the mixed diamond, the strip property, and confluence. What would close it: that the residuals of a peeled original step reassemble into one step, which held on every configuration tried (MPSS/compression-probe.py).

items.anchor: Lemma 31 · substitution for a ≤-bound name, as printed
items.html: Open and unattempted. The proved form substitutes for a name the context does not bind, which is what the β-rule's body premise needs; the printed form, with the name bound by x ≤ t, is used by nothing in the development. Lemma 32, the ≡-bound form, is proved as printed.

8.defect: quantified over every logical context, and a prevalid context may define a recursive type: in R ≡ ω ω the instance δ ≤*wf λx≤R. R x under □ δ fails

attempts.what: Search at term size 3: contexts of one or two entries over six annotation shapes, every locally closed term, every well-subtyping pair with the side conditions, four covariant contexts, the conclusion tested through the machine relation under caps.
attempts.why: 561,145 instances; three failures at chain depth 4, all joining at depth 6. The joins needed are the ‘operand reaches the bound’ chains the structural analysis predicts.
attempts.because: A counterexample at small size would settle the paper's open problem cheaply.

attempts.what: Search at term size 5, single-layer contexts.
attempts.why: 11,698,280 instances on 32 of 133 contexts, no failure; the remaining 101 contexts unsearched.
attempts.because: Size 3 is too small for the self-application patterns the structural analysis predicts.

attempts.what: Reduce the conjecture to one congruence, AppCongr₁, and locate its content: a promotion of the outermost parameter is the conjecture again on a pair of derivations of strictly smaller nesting depth.
attempts.why: The recursive instance's hypothesis is derivable and its next application well-formed; the candidate measure is the nesting depth of well-formedness premises. Steps 1–2 of the plan (a depth measure the assembling operations do not increase; lifting a ≤wf layer to the stack) are mechanizable now; steps 3–4 are the conjecture.
attempts.because: The search found nothing, and the joins it needed had a shape suggesting a measure on the derivations.

attempts.what: The reflection question: is every machine chain between well-formed ends a well-subtyping chain? Searched at sizes 3 and 5.
attempts.why: All 8,271 pairs at size 3 and all 569,295 at size 5 are well-subtyping-related; the shortest machine chain can pass through a non-well-formed term, so a proof must construct a detour. If reflection holds, the conjecture can be proved in the machine relation, where commutation and confluence are available.
attempts.because: Proving the conjecture in the machine relation would give access to commutation and confluence, which the well-subtyping relation lacks.

attempts.what: Reduce the conjecture to two obligations (Lemmas 8a, 8b and 8c): a promotion under λx≤t replayed when the parameter meets an operand (FunLift), and one under a parameter already bound to an operand replayed with more stack (FOpLift).
attempts.because: Both sides β-reduce to substituted bodies, and what remains is Lemma 9 on the substituted body, whose covariant case is the conjecture again for the operand and the annotation — with Lemma 7 needed for the substituted body's well-formedness.
attempts.why: The mutual induction of the conjecture with Lemmas 7 and 9 is genuine. Structural recursion on the target's well-formedness derivation fails, because the recursive instance's hypotheses are Lemma 7's outputs; the nesting-depth measure of §4 is what to probe next.

attempts.what: Does the nesting depth of the well-formedness derivations descend along the recursion? Minimal depths computed level by level for every term and chain to size 5, and tested on chains, Conjecture 8, Lemmas 7 and 9, β-contraction and the recursion's own round.
attempts.because: CONJ8.md §7 left it as the next thing to probe: the measure survives only if Lemma 7 and the conjecture return derivations no deeper than their inputs.
attempts.why: It does not. With y ≡ λ⊤.0, f = λx≤y. x (y x) and v = y (y y), the instance (f v, f′ v) has depth 3 and its recursive instance (v (y v), y (y v)) depth 4: an application is one deeper than its operand, and substitution copies the operand under the body's applications. 60 of 59,531 rounds go up and 6,205 stay level; Lemma 7 is bounded by the sum of its inputs' depths, not the maximum (19,361 of 151,090). Chains (568,694), Conjecture 8 at size 3 (212,584) and Lemma 9 (365,010) never need more depth than their ends. Keeping the operand in the context as x ≡ v leaves only a +1 at head positions.

attempts.what: FunLift and FOpLift without substitution, as an algorithm: narrow the parameter to the operand in the context, push the body's derivation by recursion on it, replace a promotion of the parameter by its unfolding and the lifted chain from the operand to the bound; check the resulting chain at the top level.
attempts.because: The depth probe showed that substitution is what raises the measure, and that keeping the operand in the context, as Ms-FOp does, leaves only a forced +1.
attempts.why: Valid on every instance: 2,967,285 at size 5 and 1,688,723 sampled at size 7 with stacks of up to three operands, no invalid step, no unresolved chain, no budget hit. On all 31,178 nested rounds the bound of the round is the domain of the bound of the round before — the order on which hereditary substitution terminates. The substitution route (Lemmas 7 and 9 with the context induction) does not descend in it. So the conjecture follows from well-foundedness of the domain order on well-formed bounds, a counterexample needs an infinite domain descent, and an unconditional proof along this recursion needs a normalization statement about MPSS's type level.

attempts.what: Prove the conjecture by induction on the domain rank of the target, then the context, then the chain, with the narrowing push (Lemma 8e) for each promotion and the chain at a narrowed leaf from the induction hypothesis at the bound, whose rank is lower.
attempts.because: The probe showed each round's bound is the domain of the previous round's, and that the substitution route does not descend in that order.
attempts.why: A plan, not a proof. Machine-checked: Conjecture 8 from one obligation (Lemma 8g) — the chain from the operand to the annotation when an abstraction meets an operand, in stack form under the generated side conditions; and the descent step (MPSS.DomainOrder: that annotation is the domain of the target). Owed: the obligation itself, by induction on the rank of the annotation, which needs the rank lemmas and the side condition at the points of a lifted chain proved together with the lifting. Unconditionally it needs the domain order well-founded on well-formed bounds, which MPSS's rules do not give: a well-formed T ≡wf λx≤T.⊤ would make the recursion loop. No such T is small, and a counterexample to the conjecture must contain one.

attempts.what: The converse of the rank hypothesis: MPSS plus one recursive function type, R ≡ λx≤R.R. With δ = λx≤R. x x, is f δ ≤*wf f′ δ for f = λx≤R. x δ and f′ = λx≤R. R δ?
attempts.because: The narrowing recursion descends in the domain order on bounds, and a bound whose domain is itself is the first thing that order does not handle.
attempts.why: No. Every hypothesis of the instance holds (fourteen machine steps, checked), and no chain exists: under the operand every abstraction on the head path is entered by Ms-FOp, so Ms-Pro never applies and the only promotion is Ms-Top, whose ⊤ stays; f′ δ reduces to R, an abstraction, and f δ to δ δ, which reduces to itself. 5,772 terms from f δ and 13,281 from f′ δ within length 6, none in common. Lemma 6 fails with it: (δ δ) δ is the contractum of a well-formed redex and is not well-formed. This is an extension of MPSS, not MPSS: it says the conjecture holds or fails with the existence of well-formed bounds of infinite domain rank — which the paper's §6 expects, through looping combinators.

attempts.what: The narrowing plan on p = λy≤⊤. λo≤y. λx≤(λz≤y.⊤). x o under ((□ A) a) α, A = λ⊤.⊤, a = A, α = λz≤A.z.
attempts.because: Working out the side condition at the points of a lifted chain showed that an operand's domain can depend on a parameter the abstract binders leave uninstantiated.
attempts.why: The conjecture holds at the instance — both sides β-reduce to α a and (λz≤A.⊤) a — but the narrowing algorithm promotes at (λy≤⊤. λo≤y. λx≤(λz≤y.⊤). α o) A a α, which is not well-formed: α o sits under the abstract y, where o is below y only. So the Obligation of Lemma 8g is false, step 5 of the plan is wrong, and the route that works contracts the consumed redexes first — the substitution route. The implication of Lemma 8g stands; its hypothesis does not hold.

1.account:
Open as printed; proved for the repaired reduction, and that is enough for Theorem 3. Lem-1′ in MPSS.VariantCommutation is Lemma 1 for ⟶ᵉ′, the equivalence reduction with Me-Pro's premise at the empty stack instead of the current one, by well-founded induction on the subject's size; the three cases MPSS.Commutation leaves as hypotheses (Bet-App, Fun-Fun, FOp-FOp) are proved there. The two reductions have the same reflexive-transitive closure on locally closed terms (MPSS.EmptyStackPro: every repaired step is an original step; MPSS.Peel: every original step is a chain of repaired steps), and the machine relation is closed under chains, so what is proved for ⊲′ holds for the paper's ⊲ (MPSS.VariantMachine).

The statement as printed — one original equivalence step against one promotion, joined in one step each — remains unproved, and no theorem depends on it any more. Earlier work stands: MPSS.Commutation reduces it to Lemma 2 plus four named statements, with five of the eight cases discharged outright and the Me-Pro/Ms-Pro case vacuous.

2.account:
Open as printed, and the printed induction cannot be repaired by a measure. MPSS.NoMeasure: the record of constraints a configuration measure would have to satisfy is uninhabited, since Ω's walk alternates Me-App, Me-Pro and Me-FOp forever with Me-Pro strict at every round. Refuted by counterexample, on a well-formed subject. The assumed repair is refuted as well. MPSS.Assumed carried Prop-17ʳ: the same statement with a scoping premise on the redex, at every stack. MPSS.Prop17Refuted proves ¬ Prop-17ʳ from each of the two counterexamples — the scoping premise never reaches the body, which Me-Bet opens with a fresh name. The repair therefore has to be to the rule (bind the parameter in Me-Bet's body premise, as Me-Fun and Me-FOp do) or to the statement (an operational step is a chain of equivalence steps: the witness reaches y T in two, binding and unfolding the parameter by Me-FOp, then contracting the closed body). The congruence cases lift the chain, each intermediate shown well-formed by Lemma 23 (annotations), push≡*wf (applications), or renaming under a binder (MPSS.WfRename, new). Every consumer is re-derived from it in MPSS.Preservation17, and type safety rests on Conjecture 8 alone.

changes.title: The faithfulness audit of the printed proofs
changes.summary: Every numbered result transcribed and its printed proof checked step by step. Propositions 17 and 18 refuted by counterexample; six proofs found to cite a wrong rule, a nonexistent rule, a lemma that does not cover the case, or an induction that would prove too much.

changes.title: Reflexivity with the scoping premise
changes.summary: Proposition 18 repaired as a variant: reflexivity holds once the term is scoped in the context's domain.

changes.title: Routing around the defects in Lemmas 7, 9, 33 and Proposition 27
changes.summary: The four proofs whose statements stand but whose printed arguments do not, re-proved with the right rule or the general lemma.

changes.title: Narrowing — Lemmas 23 and 24
changes.summary: Lemma 24's third conclusion proved by induction on the covariant context after the printed argument was found to prove every term well-formed; Lemma 23 on top of it, with one audit claim withdrawn along the way.

changes.title: Substitution in the three forms
changes.summary: Reduction under substitution for an unbound name, for opening, and for an ≡-bound name; the ≤-bound form the paper prints is unneeded.

changes.title: The assumed repair of Proposition 17
changes.summary: With the printed proposition refuted, its consumers were proved from an assumed statement carrying a scoping premise on the redex.

changes.title: Lemma 1 reduced to Lemma 2
changes.summary: Commutation as the paper proves it, with the diamond and three cases left as hypotheses, one of which was then discharged.

changes.title: Measures for the diamond
changes.summary: Every measure on derivations and configurations that the printed induction on Lemma 2 might use, refuted one by one, then all of them at once.

changes.title: Reformulating the diamond
changes.summary: Complete developments, erasure, confluence and a fixed configuration, each refuted as a way around the one-step diamond.

changes.title: The invariant the diamond's cases need
changes.summary: The printed second conjunct refuted and replaced by the invariant that survives the recursion; the case analysis completed against it.

changes.title: Measures on the derivations
changes.summary: Weights on promotion nodes, pair-aware weights, anchors and position orders, each surviving millions of calls and then failing.

changes.title: Searches and sweeps on the diamond
changes.summary: Counterexample searches, the recursion run on explicit trees, and structural conjectures checked by sweep.

changes.title: The promotion premise at the empty stack
changes.summary: The equivalence, subtyping and context reductions edited so that an unfolded annotation is reduced at the empty stack; the diamond and commutation proved for them, and Theorem 3 transferred to the paper's calculus through the coinciding closures.

changes.title: The mixed diamond and the reassembly question
changes.summary: One original edge against one repaired edge, joined by original steps; what is left of the printed diamond isolated and tested.

changes.title: Conjecture 8 searched and reduced
changes.summary: Searches at sizes 3 and 5, the reduction to one congruence with a nesting-depth measure, and the reflection question.

changes.title: The assumed Proposition 17 is refuted
changes.summary: The assumed statement instantiates to the refuted one, so preservation had been proved from a false hypothesis.

changes.title: Proposition 17 in chain form; type safety from Conjecture 8 alone
changes.summary: The chain of equivalence steps through well-formed terms proved for evaluation steps, with renaming for the well-formedness judgements; Proposition 27, Lemma 6 and Theorem 5 re-derived from it.

changes.title: Conjecture 8 reduced to the two binding rules
changes.summary: The abstraction congruence of well-subtyping proved; the layer walk mechanized; the conjecture, in the form the development assumes, rests on lifting a promotion under a binder whose parameter meets an operand — FunLift and FOpLift — and nothing else.

changes.title: The nesting-depth measure for Conjecture 8, probed
changes.summary: The measure proposed for the mutual induction of Conjecture 8 with Lemmas 7 and 9 — the nesting depth of well-formedness derivations — computed on all terms to size 5. It does not descend: a round of the recursion can raise it, because substitution copies the operand under the body's applications. Chains, the layer walk and Lemma 9 are depth-neutral.

changes.title: Conjecture 8 by narrowing instead of substitution
changes.summary: FunLift and FOpLift read as the machine reads them: under an operand the body is reduced under x ≡ v, so the body's derivation is narrowed and pushed by recursion on itself, and a promotion of the parameter becomes its unfolding followed by the lifted chain v ≤*wf t. Run as an algorithm and checked on 4.7 million instances; the recursion descends in the domain order on bounds.

changes.title: The narrowing route, mechanized as far as its structural half
changes.summary: Lemmas 7 and 9 from the conjecture at one pair; FunLift under one operand from the conjecture at the pair (operand, annotation); the push theorem for well-subtyping chains at a stack with the side condition as a parameter, the annotation of a plain derivation for it, and Conjecture 8 from the one obligation that is left — the chain at an abstraction that meets an operand; the domain order and its descent step. Owed: that obligation, by induction on the domain rank of the annotation (CONJ8.md §10).

changes.title: Conjecture 8 against a recursive function type
changes.summary: In MPSS extended by the one definition R ≡ λx≤R.R, which prevalidity forbids, the conjecture fails at f = λx≤R. x δ, f′ = λx≤R. R δ, δ = λx≤R. x x under the operand δ, and evaluation stops preserving well-formedness. So the conjecture is tied to the absence of bounds of infinite domain rank, which a type-level looping combinator would supply.

changes.title: The narrowing route fails on dependent bounds
changes.summary: An instance with a bound that mentions a parameter instantiated by an earlier operand: the conjecture holds, by β-reducing first, but the narrowing algorithm's intermediate point is ill-formed and the Obligation of Lemma 8g is false there.

changes.title: Conjecture 8 refuted as stated, with Lemmas 6 and 7 and Theorem 5
changes.summary: Contexts are only required to be prevalid. In Γ₀ = R ≡ ω ω, ω = λs≤⊤. λx≤(s s). (s s), the name R is well-formed (Wf-PrE) and R ≡ λx≤R.R. With δ = λx≤R. x x and t′ = λx≤R. R x: δ ≤*wf t′ and both δ δ and t′ δ are well-formed, but δ δ ≤*wf t′ δ fails — Theorem 3 gives a machine chain, t′ δ reduces to an abstraction, confluence makes δ δ reach one, and the class Bd of MPSS.AppClass, closed under both reductions, contains none. The same context refutes Lemma 6 (g = λx≤R. (x δ) δ: g δ ↦ (δ δ) δ, ill-formed), Lemma 7 and preservation. Machine-checked, --safe.
